Working entry (Epoch 3 — Driver reliability: turns and sends): «API-error turn end — logged as a turn end with a
closed cause code, never the error text; the instance idle again, the next send accepted». No freight block stands on
the entry (`block` view: 0 rows). Capability: `matrix#v2-16` («A turn ended by an API error ends the turn»).

- A turn the `claude` CLI ends on an API error is written to `events.ndjson` as a turn end, `turn-ended`, carrying
  a cause code from a CLOSED set. The error TEXT never reaches a log line, an event or a snapshot.

- After that turn end the instance reads `idle` (`viola list` and the board), the wheel's turn-running state is
  cleared exactly as a `Stop` clears it, a `wait` on the turn end returns, and the driver's next `send` is accepted.
  No human `pause` + `release` is needed.

- A test drives the API-error end through the fake agent and recorded or synthetic payloads. It fails on the tree
  before the fix (cap v2-16's «a test fails before the fix»).

- In: the hook registration in `plugin/hooks/hooks.json` for whatever CLI signal ends such a turn; its payload read in
  `viola-agent-claude` (the only crate that knows Claude); the cause set's neutral home in `viola-core` (no
  Claude-specific name, per the event-kind rule); the turn-end path in the `run` pump / wheel (`src/run/send/slot.rs`,
  `src/run/wait.rs`); the fake agent's ability to emit it; the architecture's event `data` contract for `turn-ended`.

- Out: the `wait` wake condition for background-task questions («`wait` wake condition»); send-confirmation whitespace
  and the readiness-gate race («Send confirmation»); the whole recorded 2.1.325 fixture set and its `viola verify
  --record` («The 2.1.325 recorded fixture set»); any live `claude` start (none is given, see below).

- [inferred] The defect, as measured 2026-10-26 on this host's own driver on claude 2.1.296 (MEASURED, per the
  directive): a turn ended in the CLI with «API Error: Connection lost mid-response» as the transcript's last
  assistant text, and NO `turn-ended` event followed because the Stop hook did not fire. `viola list` read `idle`, yet a
  `viola send` 25 minutes later was refused `not-delivered turn-running` (exit 13), and a waiter on the turn end never
  returned. Cap v2-16's `observed_gap` cites the same (V147). P3 re-reads it from the code: which state reads
  `turn-running` while the board reads `idle`.

- [inferred] HYPOTHESIS, not measured on 2.1.325 (the directive's words): a StopFailure-class hook, or the transcript's
  API-error line, is what can end such a turn. P3 re-measures the mechanism from the code and the recorded fixtures
  before the plan states it. A static read of the installed 2.1.325 bundle at the take-up (a tool's behaviour, for
  research's Platform issues) shows a `StopFailure` hook event. It is described «Fires instead of Stop when an API error
  (rate limit, auth failure, etc.) ended the turn. Fire-and-forget». Its input is `error` (matcher values `rate_limit`
  · `overloaded` · `authentication_failed` · `oauth_org_not_allowed` · `account_on_hold` (conditional) ·
  `verification_required` · `billing_error` · `invalid_request` · `model_not_found` · `server_error` ·
  `max_output_tokens` · `cloud_credential_error` · `unknown`, defaulting to `unknown`), `error_details` (optional) and
  `last_assistant_message` (optional). The connection-lost message is built with `error: "server_error"`. No recorded
  fixture holds a StopFailure payload (`fixtures/claude/` has no `StopFailure.*`), and viola registers no such hook
  today.

- [inferred] Whether StopFailure fires live on 2.1.325 for every API-error end (the connection-lost end included) is
  NOT readable statically. A dependence on undocumented `claude` behaviour is a capability-ledger row with a
  `viola verify` probe (CLAUDE.md invariant). P3/P4 decide whether this is a new ledger row, how its probe could be
  measured without forcing an API error, and whether a live reading is needed. If it is, the exact start count is a
  fork for the operator BEFORE the card (directive point 2).

- [inferred] The cause set: a closed viola set (every member named by the plan, with where it lives). The CLI's
  `error` string maps into it in `viola-agent-claude`, and a value outside it reads a fixed fallback member, never the
  CLI's string. `last_assistant_message` and `error_details` on this path are the error TEXT: they reach no
  `events.ndjson` line, no snapshot and no log line (directive point 4). The absence is proven by a probe checked
  against the plan's own test names and fixture keys before the card. Whether either reaches `detail-*.ndjson` (the
  content-bearing tier) is P3/P4's to decide against the NEVER-log floor and the security plan.

- [inferred] `turn-ended`'s `data` keys today are exactly `last_assistant_message` and `background_tasks`
  (`viola_core::EventKind::data_keys`). Adding a `cause` key is a wire-contract change to architecture §Standard
  Contracts (an expected amendment at the wrap). Readers skip and count unknown keys, so mixed binary versions stay
  readable.

- Live `claude` starts: the cap is NOT given. The plan runs on the fake agent and recorded or synthetic payloads first.
  A needed live reading is named as a count of starts, what each reads and what the chunk loses without it, and is
  asked through the overseer before the card.

- No mutation run, local or dispatched. Each new guard test carries its one-off remove-the-guard control through
  `gate.py control` under a kill deadline, the control's `case` being the test's NAME alone.

- A fold is decided at the phase: a red or a defect found at P3 folds in as an `[inferred]` item with its own
  acceptance and its files in research's lists.

- A test socket goes under the short `/tmp` root (`architecture · test-sockets-under-short-tmp-root`); a home given to
  `--record` goes through `record_home()`.

- `aa6bb5ab` (HEAD, the last wrap's flip): green, checks 7/7, wall 723 s, run ci#43759318845 (completed/success).
  Nothing red to fold.

# Phase directive — «API-error turn end» (Epoch 3's second entry, viola-0.2.0)

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `aa6bb5ab`: an API-error turn end is logged as a turn
   end with a closed cause code, never the error text; the instance reads idle again and the next send is accepted.
   The defect it answers, measured 2026-10-26 on this host's own driver, claude 2.1.296: a turn ended in the CLI
   with «API Error: Connection lost mid-response» (the transcript's last assistant text) and NO `turn-ended` event
   followed — the Stop hook did not fire; `viola list` read `idle`, yet a `viola send` 25 minutes later was refused
   `not-delivered turn-running` (exit 13), and a waiter on the turn end never returned. hypothesis, not measured on
   2.1.325: a StopFailure-class hook or the transcript's API-error line is what can end such a turn. Re-measure the
   mechanism at P3 from the code and the recorded fixtures before the plan states it.
2. Live `claude` starts: the cap is NOT given. Plan the chunk on the fake agent and recorded payloads first. If the
   plan cannot be honest without a live reading (what the live CLI emits at an API-error turn end on 2.1.325), name
   the exact count of starts, what each one reads and what the chunk loses without it — that is a fork for the
   operator, asked through the overseer BEFORE the card; do not plan around an assumed cap. The product now drives
   this builder on claude 2.1.325 (stamped `21 pass  0 fail` in the live home, 2026-11-15).
3. No mutation run, local or dispatched. Each new guard test carries its one-off remove-the-guard control through
   `gate.py control`, under a kill deadline, the control's `case` the test's NAME alone.
4. The cause code is a CLOSED set: the plan names every member and where the set lives, and the error TEXT reaches no
   log line, event or snapshot — an absence the plan proves with a probe that is checked against the plan's own
   test names and fixture keys before the card.
5. A fold is decided at the PHASE: a red or a defect found at P3 folds into this chunk as an `[inferred]` item with
   its own acceptance and its files in research's lists. If implement later meets a red that moves a plan entry, it
   stops and says so BEFORE the operator pass — the plan is revised through the phase's door, which closes at the
   pre-CI commit.
6. A test socket goes under the short `/tmp` root (`architecture · test-sockets-under-short-tmp-root`), and a home
   given to `--record` through `record_home()`.
7. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. The operator is PRESENT: a fork that is his is asked through the
   overseer. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the union's per-master lines and the
   `rows-union` line; whether the rows files were read whole or by search and what the card says of it; whether
   EVERY row the plan cites is in the union or its `*-standing.md`; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every

- **The CLI's API-error turn end (static read of the installed bundles, a tool's behaviour).** In 2.1.325
  (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.325/claude`) the hook metadata names `StopFailure`: «Fires instead of
  Stop when an API error (rate limit, auth failure, etc.) ended the turn. Fire-and-forget — hook output and exit
  codes are ignored». Its matcher values are `rate_limit`, `overloaded`, `authentication_failed`,
  `oauth_org_not_allowed`, `account_on_hold` (conditional), `verification_required`, `billing_error`,
  `invalid_request`, `model_not_found`, `server_error`, `max_output_tokens`, `cloud_credential_error` and `unknown`.
  The input is built as `{…session fields, hook_event_name:"StopFailure", error: e.error ?? "unknown", error_details,
  last_assistant_message}`, where `last_assistant_message` is the API-error message's text.
  The query loop's end: the `end_turn` / `stop_sequence` branch excludes `w?.isApiErrorMessage`, so no Stop fires,
  and the `if(w?.isApiErrorMessage){…return $et(Ke??w,T),{reason:"api_error",…}}` branch calls the StopFailure
  dispatcher (`$et` → `Cgs`, not awaited). The dispatcher returns early for a subagent context,
  `settingsHooksOff`, a `resume_cache_warm` query or no registered StopFailure hook. Four exhaustion paths
  (`autocompact_thrashing` ×2, prompt-too-long ×2, `malformed_tool_use_exhausted`, `empty_completion`) call it too.
  The connection-lost text («Connection lost mid-response. The response above may be incomplete.») is built with
  `error:"server_error"`.

  functions of the same name) and the byte count of `StopFailure` per bundle: 2.1.287 17 · 2.1.296 17 ·
  2.1.302 18 · 2.1.325 18, the «Fires instead of Stop» description present in each. So the hook exists on every
  stamped version, the measured 2.1.296 included, and viola has simply never registered it.
